meta.scope: LRQA Technical Support Visit - Fire Safety, Electrical Safety and Structural Safety

findings.requirement: Certificates of Occupancy issued for each building and on file
findings.observation: No occupancy certificate available for any building; factory has not yet applied to the relevant authority.
findings.code: BNBC 2020 Part 2 (Administration) - Occupancy Certificate; Fire Service & Civil Defence requirement. LRQA note: factory to communicate with the relevant authority.
findings.plain: Before a building may be used, the authority must certify that it was built as approved and is safe to occupy. Every building on the premises needs this certificate on file.
findings.evidence: Copy of renewed licence or authority acknowledgement receipt; correspondence log with the issuing authority; licence validity register

findings.requirement: Structural members carry required fire-resistance rating; members in good condition
findings.observation: Elastic Shed, Yarn Dyeing, Warehouse-A, Warehouse-B Operation Area, Connecting Shed, WTP, Workshop and Car Parking Shed are non-rated steel structures. Design philosophy establishing the applicable construction type per BNBC 2020 not provided.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Chapter 3. BNBC 2020: Part III Chapter 3 Table 3.3.1(a); Part III Section 2 Tables 3.2.2 and 3.2.3; Part IV Section 1 Table 4.1.1; Part 3 Table 3.1.7 (construction type).
findings.plain: The code sets how many hours a beam, column or wall must survive a fire without failing, based on the building's declared construction type. The factory must first establish the construction type by design philosophy, then prove each structure meets the matching rating.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Openings and penetrations through rated walls / assemblies protected
findings.observation: Rated floor assemblies penetrated by cable risers and trays on all floors of Printing, Utility and Canteen Buildings. Unprotected floor opening in Yarn Dyeing between GF and 1F (mezzanine exceeds one third of floor area, therefore a first floor). Exterior wall rating between Warehouse-A, Connecting Shed and Warehouse-B Operation Area non-compliant.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Table 3.2.3; Part 4 Sec.2.5. BNBC 2020: Part III Ch.2 Table 3.2.3; Part IV Ch.2 Sec.2.5. NFPA 101 (2012) 8.3.5 / (2018) 8.3.4 - penetrations. Doors: NFPA 80 and NFPA 252; BNBC 2020 Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.7.5 (ASTM E152). Windows: NFPA 257; BNBC 2020 Part IV Ch.1 Sec.1.5 (ASTM E163). Ducts and dampers: NFPA 90A.
findings.plain: Any hole cut through a fire-rated wall or floor - for cables, pipes or ducts - must be sealed with a tested fire-stop so the barrier still holds back fire and smoke for its full rated time. Doors and windows set into those barriers must themselves be tested fire-rated products.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Each floor separated by fire-resistive rated construction barrier
findings.observation: Cable riser and tray penetrations across all floors of Printing, Utility and Canteen Buildings; unprotected vertical opening in Yarn Dyeing between GF and 1F.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Table 3.3.1. BNBC 2020: Part III Chapter 3 Tables 3.3.1(a) and 3.3.1(b); Part IV Chapter 1 Table 4.1.1.
findings.plain: Each floor must act as a fire-resistant lid so a fire on one level cannot spread to the level above. A mezzanine larger than one third of the floor area counts as a full floor and must be separated the same way.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Separations between hazards provided with rated construction barriers
findings.observation: No rated separation for: colour mixing room and store (Printing GF); office area (Printing 3F); cooking area vs dining (Canteen 2F); storage on Canteen 3F not permitted in assembly occupancy; LPG installation east of Canteen; large storage inside Elastic Shed production area; Warehouse-A vs Warehouse-B Operation Area; flammable chemicals inside Yarn Dyeing production area.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Table 3.3.1; Part 3 Table 3.2.1 (mixed occupancies). BNBC 2020: Part III Ch.2 Sec.2.3, Tables 3.2.1, 3.2.2 and 3.2.3; Part III Ch.3 Tables 3.3.1(a) and 3.3.1(b).
findings.plain: Where a higher-risk activity sits beside a lower-risk one - cooking next to dining, chemical mixing next to production, LPG against a canteen, bulk storage inside a production hall - a rated wall or floor must separate them so a fire in the risky area stays there.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Exit enclosures provided with fire-resistive rated barriers
findings.observation: Yarn Dyeing 1F exit enclosure not protected by continuous rated assemblies. Fire doors at exit enclosures in Printing, Canteen and Utility Buildings have bottom clearance exceeding the NFPA 80 maximum, defeating the rated assembly.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Table 3.3.1 (enclosure of fire exits). BNBC 2020: Part III Ch.3 Table 3.3.1(a). NFPA 101 (2018) Sec.7.1.3 (separation of means of egress); fire barriers tested to ASTM E119.
findings.plain: The stairway people escape through must be a sealed fire-proof box from the top floor down to the exit door. A gap under a fire door larger than the tested limit lets smoke into that box and defeats the entire enclosure.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Shafts provided with minimum fire-resistance rating
findings.observation: Lift shaft at Stair 3 of Printing Building not separated from the exit enclosure by rated construction. Yarn Dyeing floor assemblies lack rated separation between successive floors, producing unprotected vertical openings.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Table 3.3.1. BNBC 2020: Part III Chapter 3 Table 3.3.1(a) - enclosure of vertical exits, exit passageways, hoistways and shafts.
findings.plain: Lift shafts and other vertical openings act as chimneys in a fire. They must be enclosed in rated construction with rated doors, and must not open directly into an escape stairway.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Standpipe system installed and functional; design/drawing reflects as-built condition
findings.observation: Class III standpipes in Printing, Canteen and Utility Buildings tested functional. Hydraulic calculation provided for Printing only, based on a 4.5 bar most-remote outlet pressure, insufficient to establish system demand; no nodal analysis and no fitting friction losses. As-built drawings inconsistent with site; hydraulically most remote hose connection not identified on layout or riser diagram; no isometric drawing; no hydrostatic pressure test report.
findings.code: NFPA 14 (2019 Edition); IBC (2018) Section 905, Art.905.3.1 - applicable for new building construction.
findings.plain: A standpipe is the riser firefighters connect their hose to. The code requires a hydraulic calculation proving enough pressure and flow reaches the furthest and highest outlet, drawings that match what is actually installed, and a hydrostatic test proving the pipework holds pressure.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Standpipe class designed per NFPA 14 for the building type
findings.observation: Class III standpipe provided at all required locations, but hydraulic calculation limited to Printing Building at 4.5 bar most-remote outlet pressure.
findings.code: NFPA 14 (2019 Edition) Chapter 5 - requirements for Class I, Class II or Class III standpipes.
findings.plain: The standpipe class determines the hose outlet type and size required. Class III serves both trained occupants and the fire service, and the design must be proven by calculation for every building, not assumed from one.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Standpipe signage installed at required locations and components
findings.observation: Standpipe signage provided at various locations, but signage identifying the most remote point and the hydraulic calculation nameplate not found.
findings.code: NFPA 14 (2019 Edition) Chapter 6.
findings.plain: Permanent signs must identify the standpipe, its hydraulically most remote point and its design pressures, so firefighters know what the system will deliver before they rely on it.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Standpipe and hose system ITM procedures documented and current
findings.observation: ITM records for the standpipe system provided; photographic evidence of the inspections not available.
findings.code: NFPA 25 (2017 Edition) Chapter 6, Table 6.1.1.2 - Standpipe and Hose Systems.
findings.plain: Standpipes and hoses must be inspected, tested and maintained on a fixed schedule, and the records must prove the work actually happened - in practice a dated photograph alongside each checklist entry.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Listed and functional fire pump provided as required
findings.observation: Listed electric and diesel fire pumps, 1000 GPM at 10 bar, positive suction, performed satisfactorily at 100% and 150% of rated flow. Deficiencies: pump room ventilation inadequate per NFPA 20; no valid flow-meter calibration certificate; no NFPA 22 inspection/maintenance records for the water storage tank; hydraulic calculation inadequate to establish system demand.
findings.code: NFPA 20 (stationary fire pumps); NFPA 22 (water storage tanks); NFPA 25 (testing).
findings.plain: The fire pump is the heart of the firefighting system. It must be a listed unit in a properly ventilated room, flow-tested with a calibrated meter, and backed by a maintained water storage tank with its own inspection records.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Fire pump ITM procedures documented and current
findings.observation: Fire pump ITM records provided; photographic evidence of inspections not available.
findings.code: NFPA 25 (2017 Edition) Chapter 8 - Fire Pumps.
findings.plain: Fire pumps require weekly churn tests and an annual flow test, all documented with evidence a third party can verify.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Fire alarm and detection system installed, functional and matching as-built drawings
findings.observation: No detection coverage at Car Parking Shed, Wastage Recycling Shed and the Canopy of Yarn Dyeing & Elastic Shed. CFDS installation in Warehouse-A and Chemical Warehouse not compliant with NFPA 72. Beam detector failed functional test. One FACP not in normal operating condition. As-built drawings for Elastic Shed and Yarn Dyeing illegible and inaccurate; battery calculation, voltage-drop calculation and testing & commissioning reports require revision.
findings.code: NFPA 72 - National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code.
findings.plain: Every occupied and hazardous area needs detection coverage, detectors must be installed exactly as their listing requires, panels must sit in normal condition, and the as-built drawings, battery and voltage-drop calculations must match the system actually installed.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Fire extinguishers inspected, tested and maintained
findings.observation: Inspection records available; inspection photo evidence not available; no record of annual servicing-agent maintenance; no record of annual CO2 extinguisher nozzle testing.
findings.code: NFPA 10 (2018 Edition) Chapter 7 - inspection, maintenance and recharging.
findings.plain: Extinguishers need a monthly quick check by trained staff and a full annual service by a competent servicing agent, with CO2 units additionally requiring an annual nozzle test. Both must be evidenced.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Notification and initiation devices installed per occupancy type
findings.observation: Same coverage and compliance gaps as FPS021: uncovered sheds and canopy, non-compliant CFDS in Warehouse-A and Chemical Warehouse, failed beam detector, one FACP off-normal, illegible as-builts.
findings.code: NFPA 72 - National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code.
findings.plain: Sounders, strobes and manual call points must be placed so that every occupant is alerted wherever they are working. The required placement is set by the occupancy type, not by convenience or cost.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Chemicals and flammable materials stored within approved enclosures
findings.observation: Colour mixing room (Printing GF) not separated from production by rated construction; flammable chemicals inside Yarn Dyeing production area without fire separation; LPG storage/installation east of Canteen not adequately separated.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Section 2.13. BNBC 2020: Part III Ch.2 Sec.2.3 and 2.14; Part VII Ch.2 Sec.2.2.5.2.2; chemical storage per BNBC Part 3 Sec.2.13, Tables 3.2.1 and 3.2.7.
findings.plain: Flammable liquids, chemicals and LPG must be kept in a purpose-built separated store - not in the production hall and not against an occupied building - with the separation rated for the quantity held.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Emergency egress maps posted at each exit stair / main point of egress
findings.observation: Egress maps posted throughout, but discrepancies between posted maps and actual site conditions at several locations including Warehouse-A and Printing Building 3F.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 Appendix A. BNBC 2020: Part IV Appendix A (Fire Safety Plan).
findings.plain: The evacuation map at each stair must show the actual layout and the actual route. A map that no longer matches the floor sends people the wrong way in smoke.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Fire Department pre-planning completed
findings.observation: Pre-planning document available but expired; renewal application submitted to local FS&CD on 20 April 2026.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 A 4.7 (Fire Safety Plan). BNBC 2020: Part IV Appendix A Section A.6 (Fire Safety Plan).
findings.plain: The local Fire Service must hold a current pre-plan for the site so they arrive already knowing the layout, hydrant points and hazards. An expired pre-plan is treated as no pre-plan.
findings.evidence: Copy of renewed licence or authority acknowledgement receipt; correspondence log with the issuing authority; licence validity register

findings.requirement: Fire drills conducted at required intervals
findings.observation: Fire drills not conducted on a monthly basis as required by BNBC 2020.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 Section A 3 and Section 1.4 (Fire Drill). BNBC 2020: Part IV Appendix A Sections A.3, A.7, A.8; Part IV Chapter 1 Section 1.4.
findings.plain: A fire drill must be run every month, covering every shift, with the evacuation time recorded and the lessons acted on.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Written housekeeping policy established and enforced
findings.observation: Housekeeping policy documented, but physical site condition shows the policy is not being enforced.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 D 20 (Housekeeping). BNBC 2020: Part IV Appendix A Section A.9.1; Part VII Chapter 2 Section 2.1.4.
findings.plain: A housekeeping policy is only compliant if the floor condition matches it. Waste, rejects and in-process material must be controlled daily, not merely described in a document.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Fire doors inspected and tested quarterly
findings.observation: Fire door inspection documents found, but the physical condition of the rated doors indicates the inspections are not being carried out effectively.
findings.code: NFPA 80 (2019 Edition) Chapter 5 - care and maintenance of fire doors.
findings.plain: Fire doors must be inspected and function-tested on a set cycle, checking closing action, latching, gaps and the absence of holes or field modifications. A signed record beside an uncorrected door means the inspection was not real.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: All applicable permits current, including Fire and Boiler Licence
findings.observation: Fire Licence, Factory, Trade, Electrician, Chemical and Boiler Licences produced. Fire Licence and BERC Licence expired and not yet renewed; renewal applications submitted.
findings.code: Licences issued by the local authority - Fire Licence (FS&CD), Factory, Trade, Electrician, Chemical, Boiler and BERC Licences.
findings.plain: Every statutory licence must be valid on the day of assessment. An application in progress is mitigation, not compliance - the acknowledgement receipt must be retained and the renewal actively chased.
findings.evidence: Copy of renewed licence or authority acknowledgement receipt; correspondence log with the issuing authority; licence validity register

findings.requirement: Aisles provide minimum unobstructed clear width of 0.9 m
findings.observation: Aisles partially blocked with materials at Printing Building, Elastic Shed, Warehouse-A and Yarn Dyeing.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Chapter 23 Section 23.2.3.2. BNBC 2006: Part 4 Sec.3.7 and Table 4.3.2 (corridors). BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.7 and Table 4.3.2.
findings.plain: Aisles must stay at least 0.9 m clear at all times so people can move at evacuation speed. Material parked in an aisle even temporarily is a non-conformity.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Means of egress minimum ceiling height 2.3 m; projections not below 2.03 m
findings.observation: Exit height at the roof level of Printing Building and Utility Building below the required minimum clearance.
findings.code: BNBC 2020: Part IV Chapter 3 Section 3.7.3. NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.1.5 (Headroom).
findings.plain: Escape routes need at least 2.3 m headroom, and 2.03 m under ducts, beams and on stairs, so people are not forced to duck or crawl while moving fast.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Exit discharge direct to exterior; discharge does not re-enter a building
findings.observation: Yarn Dyeing 1F exit discharge is into the ground floor rather than directly to the exterior. Warehouse-A north-side and Warehouse-B Operation Area south-side discharges enter the Connecting Shed without required fire separation.
findings.code: IBC (2015/2018 Edition) Section 1028 - Exit Discharge.
findings.plain: Once a person leaves the stairway they must reach open air and a public way. A discharge that puts them back inside another part of the building has not completed the escape.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Travel distance to an exit within the maximum for the occupancy
findings.observation: Travel distance in Yarn Dyeing approximately 75 m and in Warehouse-A exceeds the BNBC 2020 maximum.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 Section 3.15.1. BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.15.1, 3.15.2, Table 4.3.8. NFPA 101 (2018) Sec.7.5.4, Sec.40.2.6, Tables 40.2.6.1 and 42.2.6.
findings.plain: The code caps how far a person may have to walk to reach an exit, because that distance sets how long they are exposed to smoke. Exceeding it is fixed by adding exits or re-routing, never by signage.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Not less than two means of egress from any floor unless single exit permitted
findings.observation: Utility Building has a single exit stair serving all floors; 41 occupants observed on the second floor with the first floor unoccupied, so single-exit compliance could not be verified.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 Section 3.4 and Section 3.14.3. BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.14 and Sec.3.9. NFPA 101 (2018) Sec.7.4 (Number of Means of Egress) and Sec.7.5 (Arrangement).
findings.plain: Every floor needs two separate ways out so a single fire cannot trap people. A single stair is permitted only within strict limits on occupant numbers and travel distance, and that must be demonstrated on paper.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: All paths of egress provided with compliant illumination
findings.observation: Backup power supply for exit signs and emergency lighting could not be verified; the entire emergency power system shut down whenever the AC supply was interrupted.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 Sec.3.16; Part 8 Sec.1.5. BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.16; Part VIII Ch.1 Sec.1.2.7.
findings.plain: Escape routes must stay lit when the mains supply fails. If the backup dies with the mains, the route goes dark at exactly the moment it is needed.
findings.evidence: Load test and 90-minute discharge test report with lux readings at each egress point; circuit schedule showing life-safety loads; dated photographic evidence

findings.requirement: Means of egress free from impediments, obstructions and stored materials
findings.observation: Means of egress found obstructed by stored materials during the visit.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.1.9 (Impediments to egress) and Section 7.1.10 (Means of egress reliability).
findings.plain: The escape route must be usable instantly, without moving anything. Storage on a route is treated as seriously as a locked exit door.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Emergency power for egress illumination verified annually; 90-minute functional test
findings.observation: ITM records for the emergency lighting system provided, but they do not verify required illumination levels along all egress paths or a minimum 90-minute battery backup.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.9.3 (Periodic Testing of Emergency Lighting Equipment) and Section 7.10.9 (Testing and Maintenance).
findings.plain: Emergency lights must be proven to run for 90 minutes and to deliver the required light level along the whole route. A record without lux readings and a timed discharge does not demonstrate either.
findings.evidence: Load test and 90-minute discharge test report with lux readings at each egress point; circuit schedule showing life-safety loads; dated photographic evidence

findings.requirement: Egress doors have minimum width and required ratings
findings.observation: Door widths compliant; required fire ratings not provided at Yarn Dyeing, the north exit of Warehouse-A and the south exit of Warehouse-B Operation Area.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.2.1.2.3 (Minimum Door Leaf Width). BNBC 2006: Part 4 Sec.3.9.3. BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.9.3.
findings.plain: Escape doors must be wide enough for the occupant load and, where they sit in a rated wall, must carry a matching fire rating. A correctly sized but unrated door leaves the barrier incomplete.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Illuminated exit signs at exits and along egress where direction changes
findings.observation: Directional signs provided at several locations, but illumination level and backup supply could not be verified; exit lighting shut down on AC interruption. Verification limited because about 30% of Printing 3F, 90% of Utility 1F and 100% of Security 1F were unoccupied.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 Sec.3.16.1.1 (Location). BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.16.1.1. NFPA 101 (2018) Sec.7.10.1.2.2. NFPA 170 (symbols).
findings.plain: Illuminated exit signs must appear at every exit and at each point where the route turns or the way out is not obvious, and must stay lit on backup power.
findings.evidence: Load test and 90-minute discharge test report with lux readings at each egress point; circuit schedule showing life-safety loads; dated photographic evidence

findings.requirement: Changes in elevation of walking surfaces within 6.35 mm unless bevelled
findings.observation: Elevation changes exceed the 1/4 inch limit at several locations in the Elastic Shed and along the Printing Building roof egress path; uneven walking surfaces on the north egress path of Warehouse-B Operation Area and the Chemical Warehouse.
findings.code: BNBC 2020: Part IV Chapter 3 Section 3.3.5(a). NFPA 101 (2018) Section 7.1.7 (Changes in Level) and Section 7.1.6.2 (Changes in Elevation).
findings.plain: A step or lip greater than about 6 mm on a walking surface is a trip hazard during evacuation. Anything larger must be bevelled at 1 in 2 or rebuilt level.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Illuminated exit signs provided with battery backup and continuously illuminated
findings.observation: Illumination level and backup power for exit signs could not be verified; exit lights shut down whenever the AC supply was interrupted.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.10.5.2 - Continuous Illumination.
findings.plain: Exit signs must be lit continuously and must have their own battery or a connection to the emergency supply, so they remain readable during a power failure.
findings.evidence: Load test and 90-minute discharge test report with lux readings at each egress point; circuit schedule showing life-safety loads; dated photographic evidence

findings.requirement: Emergency power for exit signs tested annually; 90-minute functional test
findings.observation: ITM records for the exit lighting system provided, but do not demonstrate required illumination at all locations or 90-minute battery backup.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.9.3 and Section 7.10.9.
findings.plain: Exit sign backup power must be tested monthly where battery-operated and given a full 90-minute functional test once a year, with the result recorded.
findings.evidence: Load test and 90-minute discharge test report with lux readings at each egress point; circuit schedule showing life-safety loads; dated photographic evidence

findings.requirement: Exit signs have appropriate illumination levels and contrasting graphics
findings.observation: Exit sign illumination could not be verified; exit lighting shut down on AC interruption. Minimum 50 lux to be assured at all times.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 8 Section 1.5 (Illumination of Exit Signs and Means of Escape). BNBC 2020: Part VIII Chapter 1 Section 1.2.7.
findings.plain: Exit signs must reach a minimum illumination of 50 lux with contrasting lettering, so they can be read from a distance and through smoke.
findings.evidence: Load test and 90-minute discharge test report with lux readings at each egress point; circuit schedule showing life-safety loads; dated photographic evidence

findings.requirement: Stair treads of nominal uniformity
findings.observation: Non-uniform stair dimensions at one location on the stairway from the third floor to the roof of the Printing Building; riser combination non-compliant with the required uniformity.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 3 Section 1.12.5.2. BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Tables 4.3.5 and 4.3.7; Part III Ch.1 Sec.1.14.5.2.
findings.plain: Every riser and tread in a flight must be the same dimension. An odd step is the commonest cause of falls when people descend a stairway at speed.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Landings provided on both sides of egress doors; doors do not swing over stairs
findings.observation: Landings not provided on both sides at the ground floor of the Utility Building.
findings.code: BNBC 2020: Part IV Chapter 3 Section 3.9. IBC (2015/2018) Section 1010.1.5 (Floor elevation) and Section 1010.1.6 (Landings at doors).
findings.plain: There must be a level landing on both sides of an escape door, and the door must not swing out over a stair. Otherwise a person stepping through the door steps straight into a drop.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Handrails on both sides of each stairway at compliant height
findings.observation: Handrails provided on both sides in all buildings except the Security Building; intermediate rail spacing must not allow a 100 mm sphere to pass.
findings.code: NFPA 101 Section 7.2.2.4.4 and NFPA 101 (2018) Section 7.2.2.4.5 (Handrail Details). BNBC 2006: Part 4 Sec.3.10.5. BNBC 2020: Part IV Sec.3.10.4 and Sec.3.10.8.
findings.plain: Handrails are required on both sides of every stair at 760 to 1100 mm height, with intermediate rails spaced so a 100 mm sphere cannot pass through - a guard against both falls and small persons slipping through.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Exterior exit stairs separated from the building with required rating
findings.observation: Exterior stair of the Security Building not separated from the building with the required rating (rating to extend 3.05 m beyond the ends of the stair).
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.2.2.5.2 (Exposures). BNBC 2006: Part 4 Sec.3.10.8. BNBC 2020: Part IV Ch.3 Sec.3.10.11.
findings.plain: An external escape stair must be shielded from the building's own windows and walls by rated construction extending 3.05 m past the stair, so flames venting from the building cannot cut off the stair.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Interior exit stairways terminate at an exit discharge or rated passageway
findings.observation: Exit discharge from Yarn Dyeing 1F does not discharge directly to the exterior; it discharges into the ground floor.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.7.2 - Exit Discharge Through Interior Building Areas.
findings.plain: An internal escape stair must end at a door to the outside, or at a fully rated passageway leading outside. Ending inside an occupied floor puts escaping people back into the fire area.
findings.evidence: Rated-assembly design by qualified fire protection engineer; listed material / product certificates; before-and-after photographs; installation completion certificate

findings.requirement: Stair designation signs at each floor entrance in English and Bengali
findings.observation: Stair designation signs posted at all available floors in the local language only.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Part 4 Section A 4.3 (Stair and Elevator Identification). BNBC 2020: Part IV Appendix A Section A 5.3. NFPA 101 (2018) Section 7.2.2.5.4 (Stairway Identification).
findings.plain: Each stair landing needs a sign giving the stair name and floor level in both English and Bangla, so workers and attending firefighters can locate themselves inside the stairwell.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Stairwells free from stored materials and electrical appliances
findings.observation: Stored materials found in the stairwells of the Canteen and Utility Buildings; a washroom containing electrical appliances including an exhaust fan located within Exit Enclosure 1 of the Printing Building.
findings.code: NFPA 101 (2018 Edition) Section 7.1.3.
findings.plain: Nothing may be stored in a stairwell, and no other use - washrooms, electrical appliances, cupboards - may be placed inside the enclosure. Anything in there is fuel or an ignition source in the one space that must stay clear.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Rubber mats in front of substation, switchboards, distribution boards
findings.observation: Electrical rubber mats not provided in front of several switchboards and distribution boards.
findings.plain: An insulating rubber mat in front of a live panel isolates the operator from earth, so a fault cannot pass through the body to the floor. It is the last line of defence during switching.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Overhead service connections use covered conductors; underground service concealed
findings.observation: Overhead service connections are not achieved with covered conductors.
findings.plain: Overhead supply cables into the premises must be insulated (covered) conductors rather than bare wire, so contact with a person, a vehicle or a falling branch does not cause electrocution or a flashover.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Substation and generator room clean and free from combustible / stored materials
findings.observation: Table made of combustible material found inside the substation room; generator room not found clean.
findings.code: NFPA 70B (2023 Edition): Art. 11.3.2, 12.3.2, Annex B.1.13. NFPA 110 (2025 Edition): Art. 7.2.
findings.plain: Substation and generator rooms must contain nothing but the equipment. Wooden furniture, stored items, oil and dust are fuel sitting next to the highest-energy equipment on the site.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Substation and generator room have adequate ventilation
findings.observation: Transformer room and generator room have inadequate ventilation; cross ventilation not provided.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Art. 2.6.3.3, 2.6.4.2. BNBC 2020: Art. 1.3.18.3(C), 1.3.18.6, 1.3.18.7(f), 1.3.19.3. NFPA 110 (2025 Edition): Art. 7.7 Heating, Cooling and Ventilating.
findings.plain: Transformers and generators shed large amounts of heat. Cross ventilation sized by a qualified engineer is required, otherwise insulation ages rapidly and the equipment de-rates or fails.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Combustible materials not stored near electrical panels
findings.observation: Combustible materials found stored near several electrical panels.
findings.code: NFPA 70B (2023 Edition): Annex B.1.13.
findings.plain: Cartons, fabric and packaging near a panel turn a small arc into a fire. A clear, marked zone must be kept around every electrical panel.
findings.evidence: Marked and cleared area photographs (before/after); revised floor/aisle layout; housekeeping audit record; toolbox talk attendance sheet

findings.requirement: Transformer and generator body earthed at two separate points; neutral earthed separately
findings.observation: Earthing design not prepared to standard. System/body earthing and neutral earthing not isolated. Transformer and generator body and neutral earthing not connected to the required number of earth conductors. Design methodology/philosophy missing.
findings.code: Bangladesh Electricity Rules 1937: Clause 57. Handbook of Electrical Power Distribution by G. Ramamurthy, Sec.7.14 (earthing for transformers, generator sets, motors and switchgears; recommended earth conductor).
findings.plain: Transformer and generator bodies must each be earthed at two separate points, and the neutral must be earthed at its own separate point. Mixing body and neutral earthing means a fault can energise the equipment casing.
findings.evidence: Earthing/LPS design report with calculation and methodology; pit and layout drawing; earth resistance and continuity test report

findings.requirement: All equipment efficiently earthed and connected to required number of earth electrodes
findings.observation: Equipment not efficiently earthed or connected to the required number of earth electrodes; earthing design not prepared to standard; system/body and neutral earthing not isolated; design methodology missing.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Art. 2.8.1, 2.8.3, 2.11.5.1. BNBC 2020: Art. 1.3.32, 1.3.42.3(v). NFPA 70 (2023 Edition): Art. 110.54(B). G. Ramamurthy Handbook Sec.7.14.
findings.plain: Every metal enclosure must have a low-resistance path to earth through the correct number of electrodes, so a fault trips the breaker instead of leaving the casing live. The number of electrodes must come from a calculation, not a rule of thumb.
findings.evidence: Earthing/LPS design report with calculation and methodology; pit and layout drawing; earth resistance and continuity test report

findings.requirement: Switchboards / distribution boards installed in compliant locations
findings.observation: Some switchboards and distribution boards are not installed in compliant locations (1 m front clearance, mounting height, proximity to washing units and stoves).
findings.plain: A panel needs at least 1 m of clear working space in front, must sit between 0.45 m and 2 m above the floor, and must not be above a stove or sink or within 2.5 m of a washing unit - so it can be operated safely and is not exposed to water or heat.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Internal components of boards concealed and free of dust and debris
findings.observation: Most switchboards and distribution boards not properly concealed; some panels sealed with silicone with no documentation proving the sealing material is non-combustible and fire resistant.
findings.plain: Live parts must sit behind covers and blanking plates, and the enclosure must be dust-proof and vermin-proof in non-combustible material. Silicone used as a seal needs a certificate proving it is fire resistant.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Boards have clear identification markings and capacity information labels
findings.observation: Most switchboards and distribution boards lack clear and permanent identification marks and capacity information labels.
findings.plain: Each board and each circuit must carry a permanent label stating what it feeds and its rating, so that in an emergency the correct circuit is isolated first time.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: No indication of overheating, overloading or signs of burning
findings.observation: Indications of overheating observed: one Category-2 and two Category-1 hotspots.
findings.code: NFPA 70B (2023 Edition): Art. 7.4, Chapters 16 and 24. NETA MTS 2019: Table 100.18.
findings.plain: Thermographic categories rank how far above normal a connection is running: Category 1 needs monitoring, Category 2 needs repair at the next opportunity, Category 3 is immediate. Each is a loose or overloaded joint heading toward an arc fire.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Each circuit provided with a dedicated neutral
findings.observation: Neutral cables not identified, so provision of dedicated neutrals could not be determined.
findings.plain: Each circuit needs its own neutral. Sharing neutrals between circuits overloads the shared conductor and can leave it live even when the circuit breaker is switched off.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Electrical wiring / cables properly identified
findings.observation: Most electrical cables are not properly identified by colour coding, marking tape or tagging.
findings.plain: Cables must be identifiable by colour, marking tape or tag, so anyone working on the system knows which conductor is phase, neutral and earth before touching it.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Wiring / cables sized according to circuit breaker capacity
findings.observation: Most circuit breakers are not sized according to the capacity of the connected loads.
findings.plain: The breaker must trip before the cable overheats. The rule is cable rating >= breaker rating >= circuit load; a breaker larger than its cable means the cable burns while the breaker holds.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: No multi-looping of wiring at circuit breakers within boards
findings.observation: Multi-looping and bunched cables observed at circuit breakers within some switchboards and distribution boards.
findings.plain: One conductor per terminal. Looping several cables into a single breaker terminal creates a loose, high-resistance joint - the commonest origin of panel fires.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Phase separators provided between terminals on circuit breakers
findings.observation: Phase separators not provided between terminals on some MCCBs.
findings.plain: Phase separators between breaker terminals stop a tool, a stray wire strand or vermin bridging two phases and causing a short-circuit flashover.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Electrical wiring and conduit properly supported
findings.observation: Electrical wiring and conduit not properly supported at some locations.
findings.plain: Cables and conduits must be clipped and supported at set intervals, so their weight is not carried by the terminations and so they cannot be walked on or damaged.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Cable joints through porcelain/PVC connectors with PIB tape
findings.observation: Cable joints made through connectors without PIB tape wound around the joint.
findings.plain: A cable joint must be made in a proper porcelain or PVC connector and then wrapped with PIB tape to restore the insulation and keep moisture out.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: No unprotected light fixtures in storage areas; prohibition signage installed
findings.observation: Signage prohibiting light fixtures without protective covers not installed in storage areas. Surface wiring not run in GI/metal conduit at some locations. Proper clearance not maintained from electrical equipment and fixtures such as the forklift battery charger and sockets.
findings.code: International Fire Code (2021 Edition): Art. 308.1.1. The Factories Rules 1979: Chapter 4 / Rule 53 (and Rule 1.5.3.5).
findings.plain: Bare, uncovered lamps are prohibited in storage areas because a broken hot bulb can ignite stored goods. Bilingual prohibition signage is required at every entrance, and surface wiring in stores must run inside GI or metal conduit.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Electrical connections at equipment and fixtures properly secured
findings.observation: Connections at equipment and fixtures not properly secured in some places; junction boxes and devices require adequate covers and protection from water ingress.
findings.code: NFPA 70 (2023 Edition): Chapters 2, 3 and 4. BS 7671:2018: Art. 522.3, 526.7.
findings.plain: Connections must be mechanically secure and enclosed, and wiring selected so water ingress cannot damage it. An open junction box allows accidental contact with live parts.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: All wiring properly terminated at its point of termination
findings.observation: Some cables not properly terminated (un-terminated wires, lugs not provided at terminals).
findings.plain: Stranded conductors of 6 sq mm and above need cable sockets (lugs); smaller conductors must be soldered or crimped with a ferrule. Loose strands under a screw make a hot joint and can bridge to the adjacent phase.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Mechanical guards provided for electrical equipment and wiring
findings.observation: Mechanical guards not provided for electrical equipment and wiring at some locations.
findings.plain: Cables and equipment in traffic or working areas need physical guards, so trolleys, forklifts and machinery cannot crush or cut them.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Substation and generator room accessible with sufficient maintenance clearance
findings.observation: Generator room has insufficient clearance for regular maintenance activities.
findings.plain: Enough space must be kept around a generator for routine servicing and for a technician to withdraw safely. Cramped rooms lead to skipped maintenance and unsafe working.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: Generator ITM procedures completed and documented
findings.observation: Generator inspection, maintenance and testing not completed and documented to standard or manufacturer guidelines.
findings.code: NFPA 110 (2025 Edition): Chapter 8, Annex A. NFPA 110 (2019) Annex A may be used as a reporting format.
findings.plain: The standby generator must be exercised and serviced on a documented schedule with dated photographic evidence, so it is proven to start and carry load when the mains fail.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Generator exhaust discharged to exterior in a safe location
findings.observation: Generator exhaust is not discharged to the exterior of the building in a safe location.
findings.code: BNBC 2020: Art. 1.3.19.3. NFPA 110 (2025 Edition): Art. 7.10.
findings.plain: Generator exhaust must be piped outside to a point where hot gases and carbon monoxide cannot re-enter the building or reach people or combustible material.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: UPS / IPS ITM procedures completed and documented
findings.observation: UPS and IPS inspection, maintenance and testing not completed and documented to standard or manufacturer guidelines.
findings.code: NFPA 111 (2025 Edition): Chapter 8, Annex A. NFPA 111 (2019) Ch.8 Table A.8.3.2 (procedures) and Figure A.8.4.2 (operation and testing).
findings.plain: UPS and IPS units must be tested and maintained on a documented schedule, since they are what keeps exit signs and emergency lights alive during a power cut.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Life safety loads connected to the emergency power system
findings.observation: Fire alarm and detection and fog lights on battery backup; emergency lights and exit signs on IPS; diesel pump available; the lift has no ARD or other emergency backup.
findings.plain: Life-safety loads - fire alarm, fire pump, lifts, emergency lighting and exit signs - must be fed from the emergency supply. A lift without an ARD can trap people between floors during a power failure.
findings.evidence: Load test and 90-minute discharge test report with lux readings at each egress point; circuit schedule showing life-safety loads; dated photographic evidence

findings.requirement: Appropriate type and number of firefighting equipment for substation and generator room
findings.observation: Appropriate type and number of firefighting equipment not installed for the substation and generator room.
findings.plain: Substation and generator rooms need extinguishers of a type safe on live electrical equipment (CO2 or dry powder), in the correct number for the room size.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Ground fault and overcurrent protection devices on generator or panel
findings.observation: Ground fault protection device not found where required.
findings.code: NFPA 70 (2023 Edition): Art. 230.95.
findings.plain: Ground fault protection is required on solidly grounded wye services above 150 V to earth but not exceeding 600 V phase-to-phase, where the service disconnect is rated 1000 A or more. It catches earth faults too small to trip the main breaker but large enough to start a fire.
findings.evidence: Before-and-after rectification photographs; revised panel schedule; test/thermographic rescan report; material and product certificates

findings.requirement: As-built electrical drawings available for review
findings.observation: As-built SLD does not match the installation; circuit breakers not selected on the basis of load capacity. Detailed SLD content requirements (source data, breaker/cable coordination IC >= ICB >= IL, 20% derating, 125% breaker rating, feed-from/feed-to) to be applied.
findings.plain: The single line diagram is the map of the whole electrical system. It must match the installation and must show source data, every breaker and cable with its rating, and feed-from and feed-to, applying cable rating >= breaker rating >= load, 20 per cent cable derating and a breaker rated at 125 per cent of circuit current.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Earthing drawings up to date and kept on site
findings.observation: Earthing design not prepared to standard; system/body and neutral earthing not isolated; pit layout missing; design methodology/philosophy missing.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Art. 2.8. BNBC 2020: Art. 1.3.32. NFPA 70 (2023 Edition): Art. 250.
findings.plain: The earthing drawing must state the earthing system type (TT, TN-S, TN-C, TN-C-S or IT), the calculation behind the number of earth pits and conductor size, the pit layout with pit-to-pit spacing, and the single line of earthing from pit to busbar to equipment.
findings.evidence: Earthing/LPS design report with calculation and methodology; pit and layout drawing; earth resistance and continuity test report

findings.requirement: Equipment and electrical layout drawings up to date and kept on site
findings.observation: Electrical layout drawing not prepared to standard; not every floor of every building is covered.
findings.plain: A floor-by-floor electrical layout showing every outlet, switch, circuit and cable route is what allows safe isolation, planned maintenance and emergency response. Every building and every floor must be covered.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Load Management Program established and recorded
findings.observation: No Load Management Program established or recorded. A load schedule covering panel board name, location, feed-from, breaker and cable data, incoming voltage and current and outgoing circuits, with balanced loading, is required.
findings.plain: A load schedule records what is actually connected to each panel and how the three phases are balanced. Without it, overloading and phase imbalance go undetected until something burns.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Thermographic scans every four months with hotspots remediated
findings.observation: Thermal scanning is performed but the report is not prepared properly (summary page, equipment name/location, ambient temperature, max rated load, load %, category, rescan after remediation, minimum 40% loading during survey).
findings.code: NFPA 70B (2023 Edition): Table 9.2.1, Art. 7.4. NETA MTS 2019: Table 100.18.
findings.plain: Infrared scanning finds hot joints before they fail. It must be done every four months at not less than 40 per cent of rated load, reported with equipment name, location, ambient temperature, load percentage and category, and re-scanned after every repair.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Electrical safety training delivered with documentation on site
findings.observation: Workers operating and maintaining the electrical system have received training, but no detailed training manual is available.
findings.code: NFPA 70E (2024 Edition). NFPA 70B (2023 Edition): Art. 4.3.
findings.plain: Anyone working on the electrical system must be trained against a documented manual covering electrical hazards, PPE, lock-out/tag-out, safe working live and dead, first aid and CPR. Attendance records alone do not prove the training content was adequate.
findings.evidence: Detailed training manual; attendance sheet and competency assessment; appointment/designation letter with job description

findings.requirement: Periodic safety inspections of electrical system components documented
findings.observation: Periodic safety inspection schedule not properly prepared; required items missing; the existing schedule covers factory machines only.
findings.plain: An annual electrical maintenance plan must list every item - transformer, generator, switchgear and panel boards, ATS, COS, IPS/UPS, boiler, compressor and lightning protection - with planned and actual dates. A schedule covering production machines only does not meet this.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Periodic Insulation Resistance Measurement Program established and recorded
findings.observation: IR measurement programme not carried out properly; IR not measured for each cable where multiple cables share a single terminal.
findings.plain: Insulation resistance testing measures whether cable insulation is still sound. Each conductor must be tested individually against all others - phase to phase, phase to neutral and phase to earth - because a single combined reading hides a failing core.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: Switchgear and panel boards inspected against listed ratings
findings.observation: Switchgear and panel board inspection and testing report not available (ACB/VCB/LBS, ATS/COS, transformer test and inspection reports).
findings.code: NFPA 70B (2023 Edition): Annex E Figures E.2 to E.23 (circuit breaker, disconnect switch, switchgear, panelboard, transformer and ATS report formats), Annex H, and Chapter 9 (Maintenance Intervals).
findings.plain: Switchgear, breakers, transfer switches and transformers must be inspected and tested against their listed ratings at an interval set by their condition assessment - every 12, 36 or 60 months - with a formal test report on file.
findings.evidence: Revised ITM checklist and annual schedule; completed records with dated photographic evidence; third-party servicing agent report and certificate

findings.requirement: LPS properly installed following approved design and drawing
findings.observation: No LPS drawing or installation for ETP, Transformer Room, Diesel & Generator Shed, Wastage Recycling Shed, Car Parking Shed and Warehouse Connecting Shed. LPS installed at Security Building without a drawing. LPS drawing mismatches the installation at Printing Building. External metals not bonded to ground or the LPS.
findings.code: BNBC 2006: Art. 2.9. BNBC 2020: Art. 1.3.33. NFPA 780 (2023 Edition).
findings.plain: A lightning risk index calculation determines which structures need protection. Protected structures need air terminals, down conductors and earth terminations all designed and drawn, and every external metal item must be bonded so lightning cannot side-flash into the building.
findings.evidence: Earthing/LPS design report with calculation and methodology; pit and layout drawing; earth resistance and continuity test report

findings.requirement: Floor Load Plans posted as required
findings.observation: Load plans not posted at all required locations of the multi-storied buildings.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.5 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.5.
findings.plain: A floor load plan states how much weight each area of each floor may carry. It must be prepared by a qualified structural engineer and posted where the people stacking material can actually see it.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Floor loads in compliance with posted plans
findings.observation: Load plans not posted at required locations of any of the multi-storied buildings, so compliance cannot be demonstrated.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6.
findings.plain: Actual loading on the floor must stay within the posted plan. Where no plan is posted, compliance cannot be demonstrated at all.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Storage areas marked with acceptable loading limits from the Load Plan
findings.observation: No load restriction / height marking at the Printing Building 2F storage area, Yarn Dyeing 1F and Canteen Building 3F.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6.
findings.plain: Storage areas need floor markings and stacking-height limits, so a worker can tell at a glance when a stack has reached the safe limit.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Programme in place so design live loads are not exceeded
findings.observation: No load management programme found during the visit.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6.
findings.plain: A live load management programme is the routine - who checks, how often, and what happens on exceedance - that keeps real loading inside the design assumption as production patterns change.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Designated full-time Factory Load Manager appointed and trained
findings.observation: No Load Manager has been appointed.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.4.6.
findings.plain: One named, full-time person on site must be trained to calculate operational floor loads, act as the resource for vendors, and stop overloading. It is a designated role, not a general duty spread across a department.
findings.evidence: Detailed training manual; attendance sheet and competency assessment; appointment/designation letter with job description

findings.requirement: Areas needing maintenance (efflorescence, dampness, ponding, corrosion) addressed
findings.observation: Dampness on third floor walls of the Canteen Building; standing water on the roofs of Utility, Canteen and Generator Buildings; corrosion on the Printing Building roof steel stair, the steel stair adjacent to the Security Building and the ETP steel stair.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 1 Section 1.14.13 and Chapter 3 Section 3.1.13; 2006 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 1 Section 1.12.13 and Chapter 3 Section 3.1.11.
findings.plain: Water is the main agent of structural decay. Standing water on roofs, dampness in walls and corrosion on steel must be traced to a cause and repaired under a structural engineer's direction, not simply painted over.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Expansion joints provided at appropriate intervals on the exterior facade
findings.observation: Expansion joint not provided between the walls of the Fire Pump room and WTP.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 3 Section 3.1.12 and 2006 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 3 Section 3.1.10.
findings.plain: Expansion joints let adjoining structures move independently with temperature change and settlement. Without one, the shared wall cracks and lets water in.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Expansion joint material free from cracking and deterioration
findings.observation: Expansion joint absent between the Fire Pump and WTP walls; signs of water intrusion observed on the shared wall where the joint should be.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 3 Section 3.1.12 and 2006 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 3 Section 3.1.10.
findings.plain: The joint filler must stay flexible and intact. Cracked, deteriorated or absent filler is a direct water path into the structure.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Building free from active water intrusion or ponding due to facade performance
findings.observation: Active signs of water intrusion in the Canteen Building, Utility Building and the wall between the Fire Pump and WTP.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 1 Section 1.14.13 and Chapter 3 Section 3.1.13; 2006 BNBC Part 3 Chapter 1 Section 1.12.13 and Chapter 3 Section 3.1.11.
findings.plain: The external envelope must keep water out. Active intrusion means the facade system is not performing and the structure behind it is being damaged continuously.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Performance of key structural elements satisfactory
findings.observation: Columns and transfer structures appear satisfactory on visual observation. Slender columns found in Warehouse-A. No flat plates found. A qualified structural engineer must confirm structural performance.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.9 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.9.
findings.plain: Columns, slender columns, flat plates and transfer structures carry the whole building. Where visual inspection raises a question - such as the slender columns in Warehouse-A - a qualified structural engineer must confirm capacity by calculation.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Structural steel members free of corrosion and physical damage
findings.observation: Corrosion observed on the Printing Building roof steel stair, the steel stair adjacent to the Security Building and the ETP steel stair.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 10 Section 10.12.7 and Section 10.2.3.11; 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 10 Section 10.10.4.
findings.plain: Corrosion reduces the steel section that carries the load. Affected members must be tested to measure the remaining thickness before any repair or replacement decision is made.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Non-structural elements anchored and braced against earthquake forces
findings.observation: One plastic water tank each on the roofs of the Utility Building, Printing Building and Generator Building found unanchored.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 2 Section 2.5.15.2 and Section 2.5.18; 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 2 Section 2.5.8.
findings.plain: Anything sitting on or hanging from the structure - water tanks, ducts, light fittings - must be anchored and braced, because in an earthquake unrestrained items slide off, fall and block escape routes.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Certificates of Occupancy available for review
findings.observation: Certificate of Occupancy not available for review.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 2, Chapter 3 and 2006 BNBC Part 2.
findings.plain: The Occupancy Certificate is the authority's confirmation that the building as built matches what was approved and may lawfully be used. It is the foundational document all other structural compliance rests on.
findings.evidence: Copy of renewed licence or authority acknowledgement receipt; correspondence log with the issuing authority; licence validity register

findings.requirement: Credible structural design documents available and kept on site
findings.observation: As-built mismatches: Printing Building 1F toilet buildup (13 inch) not shown on drawings and ferro-scan counts 5 rebars per face against 4 shown for grids I4, D2 at ground floor; Warehouse-A vertical cross bracing location altered between grids A and G with eave height 10 m against 9.6 m; WTP grid 3D column C2 measured 300x300 mm against 400x400 and 330x330 shown. No printed drawings for Transformer Room, Diesel & Generator, Warehouse Connecting Shed and Wastage Recycling Shed.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.9 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.9.
findings.plain: As-built drawings must show the building as it actually stands. Where the drawing says 400 mm and the column measures 300 mm, the design calculations behind that drawing no longer describe the real structure.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Structural documentation demonstrating general conformance with BNBC
findings.observation: Design report mismatches as per SSD004, plus: Elastic Shed and Warehouse-A compression struts connected to rafter top flange requiring adequacy check against the as-constructed condition; no seismic load calculation for Fire Pump, WTP and Workshop; no drawings or design report for Transformer Room, Diesel & Generator, Warehouse Connecting Shed and Wastage Recycling Shed; no design report for the Car Parking Shed; seismic design category and detailing requirements to be defined per building.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.9 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.9.
findings.plain: A design report must show, for each building, that the structure was analysed for its real loads and detailed for its assigned seismic design category. Structures with no report at all have never been demonstrated safe.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Documented compliance with BNBC seismic and wind requirements
findings.observation: No seismic load calculation in the design reports for the Pump Room, WTP and Workshop. No drawings or design report for Transformer Room, Diesel & Generator, Warehouse Connecting Shed and Wastage Recycling Shed. No design report for the Car Parking Shed. Seismic design category to be defined by site class, seismic zone and occupancy category for each building.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.5 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.5.
findings.plain: Bangladesh sits in a seismic and cyclone zone. Each building must have a seismic design category assigned from its site class, seismic zone and occupancy category, with matching earthquake and wind load calculations.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date

findings.requirement: Clear and redundant load path to resist lateral loads
findings.observation: Clear and redundant load path appears to exist in all visited buildings except the Diesel & Generator shed and the Wastage Recycling shed.
findings.code: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.5 and 2006 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.5.
findings.plain: Lateral loads from wind and earthquake must have a continuous, redundant path from roof to foundation. If any link is missing or single, the frame can unzip under sideways load.
findings.evidence: Qualified structural engineer report; load plan drawings and posted signage photographs; repair completion record with photographs

findings.requirement: Ferro-scanning confirms steel rebar in lowest tier columns
findings.observation: Ferro scan counts 5 rebars per face against 4 shown on drawings for grids I4, D2 at the ground floor of the Printing Building.
findings.code: Reinforcement details of columns at ground floor, first floor and roof top level to be determined using a scanning device (ferro-scan). Related: 2020 BNBC Part 6 Chapter 1 Section 1.9.
findings.plain: Ferro-scanning reads the reinforcement hidden inside concrete. A count that differs from the drawing means the structure's real capacity is unknown until an engineer reconciles the two.
findings.evidence: Revised and signed as-built drawing set; supporting design/hydraulic/battery calculation report; drawing register entry with revision number and date
